sources.covers: image tokens per image at 224 px (the backbone π0 is initialised from)

note: openpi resizes every image to 224 × 224 keeping its aspect ratio and pads the rest with black, split evenly on both sides (image_tools.resize_with_pad, which replicates tf.image.resize_with_pad). In training only, non-wrist images also get a random crop of 95 % of each side, a resize back and a ±5° rotation (model.preprocess_observation); not at inference. Three image slots (a base camera and two wrist cameras); a robot with fewer cameras masks the missing slots. control_hz is the paper's upper figure; its UR5e and Franka robots run at 20 Hz and execute 16 actions per chunk. Code Apache-2.0 (the Gemma weights carry Gemma's terms, LICENSE_GEMMA.txt). DexVantage bundles these figures only, not the model.

crop_rule.quote: resize_with_pad: "Resizes an image to a target height and width without distortion by padding with black"; pad_h0, remainder_h = divmod(height - resized_height, 2) (centred)

tokens_per_image.quote: "We always resize the image to a fixed square size (224, 448, or 896 pixels). This leads to a fixed number of image tokens per model variant (respectively 256, 1024, or 4096 tokens)"

n_cameras.quote: IMAGE_KEYS = ("base_0_rgb", "left_wrist_0_rgb", "right_wrist_0_rgb"); the paper: "with 2 or 3 images per robot", "we also mask out the missing image slots"

action_chunk.quote: "we use H=50 for our tasks" (openpi Pi0Config: action_horizon: int = 50)

execute_steps.quote: for 50 Hz robots "we run inference every 0.5 seconds (after executing 25 actions)"; the 20 Hz UR5e and Franka every 0.8 s, after 16 actions

temporal_ensemble_m.quote: they "tried temporal ensembling early on and found that it hurt policy performance" and execute chunks open-loop

inference_ms.quote: 73 ms on-board: image encoders 14 ms, observation forward pass 32 ms, ten flow forward passes 27 ms; 86 ms off-board with 13 ms of network latency

control_hz.quote: "control robots at frequencies of up to 50 Hz" (the UR5e and Franka at 20 Hz)
